0.0.n: Used at the start to continue the description.

0.1.n: Adds a friendly tone and draws the listener into the explanation.

0.3.n: Refers to the pictures making up the design, rather than just its colors.

0.4.n: Marks 絵柄 as the topic being described.

0.5.n: A shortened loanword commonly used for ice cream or frozen treats.

0.6.n: Links アイス and うさぎちゃん as the things pictured.

0.7.n: The following number tells us there are three; Japanese nouns do not change for plural.

0.8.n: An affectionate suffix attached to うさぎ, making the rabbits sound endearing.

0.9.n: Marks the ice cream and bunnies as what has been drawn.

0.10.n: 羽 is the counting word for birds and, traditionally, rabbits too.

0.11.n: 描く in て-form + ある describes a deliberately created result; あって connects to the next description.

0.13.n: Casual use of すごい instead of すごく strengthens the description that follows.

0.14.n: Adds conversational warmth during a pause before the color description.

0.16.n: An English loanword describing the soft, fanciful impression of the colors.

0.17.n: Connects ドリーミー to 可愛い so both describe 色味.

0.18.n: Directly describes 色味, expressing the speaker's positive impression of the colors.

0.19.n: Refers to the shades and overall impression of the colors.

0.20.n: Pairs with なっています to introduce the resulting appearance.

0.21.n: なる + ています politely describes the finished design here, rather than an ongoing change.

1.0.n: Starts another point in the product description.

1.2.n: Refers to the upper part of the item.

1.3.n: Links 上 to 方 to form an expression meaning the upper area.

1.4.n: In 上の方, 方 makes the location approximate rather than specifying an exact edge.

1.5.n: Marks the location where the glue is attached.

1.6.n: Here のり refers to adhesive, not the seaweed that shares this pronunciation.

1.7.n: Marks のり as the thing that is attached.

1.8.n: Casual shortening of 付いている, describing a state that remains after something sticks or is applied.

1.9.n: The preceding description specifies which kind of item this is.

1.10.n: Ends the sentence politely after the noun タイプ.

0.lit: And, you know, the pattern has ice cream and three bunnies drawn, and really, you know, has dreamy, cute colors.
0.tip: 描いてある describes the result of someone deliberately drawing something, not the action of drawing right now.

1.lit: And, it is the type with glue attached at the upper area.
1.tip: 付いてる directly modifies タイプ: Japanese places the whole description before the noun, without a word like that.
